description: PyBTLS is a Python interface to the C++ Bridge Traffic Load Simulation program, maintained by the PyBTLS developers. It generates traffic or reads historical vehicle records, calculates load effects using bridge influence lines or surfaces, and processes the resulting histories. Built-in analyses include block maxima, peaks over thresholds and rainflow counting. Outputs are organized in folders and can be loaded as pandas tables. Bridge geometry, vehicle populations and simulation duration are user-defined, with no fixed geographical coverage. Source code, documentation and a PyPI package are publicly available free under GPL-3.0. Python 3.10 or later and a 64-bit system are required. This supports bridge assessment, design-code calibration and investigations of extreme traffic loading. A limitation is that its simplified vehicle-following rule prevents overlap but does not represent full traffic microsimulation or lane changing. The documentation therefore recommends short-to-medium bridges or use as an input generator for a more detailed simulator. No directly related catalogue record was established, and the software was not run.
inputs: Traffic flow, volume, composition and speed assumptions or historical vehicle records
name: PyBTLS bridge traffic-load simulation
notes: G5 G5-0128. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
outputs: Block maxima, threshold exceedances and rainflow results
